title: CIA-UAP-003, The Central Intelligence Agency and Overhead Reconnaissance; The U-2 and OXCART Programs, 1954-1974
doc_notes: This document is a CIA History Staff monograph detailing the history of the U-2 and OXCART reconnaissance programs from 1954 to 1974. / This document is a history of the CIA's U-2 and OXCART reconnaissance programs from 1954 to 1974, detailing operational missions and the political context of the Cold War. / This document is a CIA history of the U-2 and OXCART reconnaissance programs from 1954 to 1974, detailing operations, organizational changes, and technical developments. / This document is a CIA History Staff account of the U-2 and OXCART reconnaissance programs from 1954 to 1974, detailing development, operational history, and program termination.

incidents.summary: Soviet fighters shot down a US Navy Privateer patrol aircraft over the Baltic Sea.
incidents.quote: Soviet fighters shot down a US Navy Privateer patrol aircraft over the Baltic Sea.

incidents.summary: Soviet aircraft downed a US Navy Neptune bomber near Vladivostok.
incidents.quote: Soviet aircraft downed a twin-engine US Navy Neptune bomber near Vladivostok.

incidents.summary: US RB-29 lost in the Sea of Japan, likely shot down by Soviet fighters.
incidents.quote: An RB-29 lost in the Sea of Japan on 13 June 1952 was probably also a victim of Soviet fighters.

incidents.summary: Soviet fighter aircraft shot down a US RB-29 flying over Hokkaido.
incidents.quote: Soviet fighter aircraft stalked and shot down a US RB-29 flying over Hokkaido.

incidents.summary: RAF Canberra overflight of the Soviet missile test range at Kapustin Yar.
incidents.quote: Soviet fighters damaged and nearly shot down the Canberra.

incidents.summary: Francis Gary Powers' U-2 shot down over the Soviet Union.
incidents.quote: the Soviet Union shot down a CIA U-2 and publicly tried its pilot, Francis Gary Powers.

incidents.summary: A U-2 on a training flight from Lakenheath inadvertently penetrated the British radar network, causing RAF fighters to scramble.
incidents.quote: a U-2 on a training flight from Lakenheath inadvertently penetrated the British radar network

incidents.summary: First operational use of a U-2 over Poland and East Germany.
incidents.quote: The first operational use of a U-2 took place on Wednesday, 20 June 1956.

incidents.summary: First overflight of the Soviet Union by U-2 Article 347.
incidents.quote: On Wednesday, 4 July 1956, the U-2 known as Article 347 began the first flight over the Soviet Union.

incidents.summary: U-2 overflight of Moscow and other targets.
incidents.quote: The second overflight, on the following day, continued the search for Bison bombers.

incidents.summary: U-2 mission 4016 over Soviet Armenia.
incidents.quote: This mission left Adana and flew east over Iran, then reversed and flew west along the Soviet-Iranian border to Soviet Armenia

incidents.summary: U-2 mission 4155 over Saryshagan and Tyuratam.
incidents.quote: mission 4155 headed first for Saryshagan, where it obtained the first pictures of two new Soviet radars

incidents.summary: Francis Gary Powers' U-2 downed by SA-2 missile near Sverdlovsk.
incidents.quote: an SA-2 surface-to-air missile detonated close to and just behind his aircraft and disabled it

incidents.summary: Francis Gary Powers' U-2 aircraft was shot down over the Soviet Union.
incidents.quote: The loss of Francis Gary Powers' U-2 over the Soviet Union on 1 May 1960

incidents.summary: A U-2 aircraft with a Nationalist Chinese pilot was shot down over the People's Republic of China.
incidents.quote: a U-2 with a Nationalist Chinese pilot was shot down over the People's Republic of China

incidents.summary: A U-2C aircraft was shot down over Cuba, killing the pilot, Maj. Rudolph Anderson.
incidents.quote: one of the U-2Cs lent by the Agency to the Air Force was shot down over Cuba

incidents.summary: A Nationalist Chinese U-2 pilot was shot down over the PRC.
incidents.quote: a second Project TACKLE U-2 was lost near the Kiangsi-Chekiang border

incidents.summary: A Nationalist Chinese U-2 pilot was shot down over the PRC.
incidents.quote: This loss came on 7 July 1964.

incidents.summary: A U-2C aircraft was shot down in the vicinity of Shanghai.
incidents.quote: The U-2C aircraft overflew central China and fell victim to a SAM in the vicinity of Shanghai

incidents.summary: A-12 crash near Wendover, Utah due to ice in pitot-static tube.
incidents.explanation: Ice plugged a pitot-static tube causing erroneous airspeed indication.
incidents.quote: The first A-12 crash occurred on 24 May 1963

incidents.summary: A-12 article 133 crash during landing due to frozen pitch-control servo.
incidents.explanation: Pitch-control servo device froze, rolling the plane into a wing-down position.
incidents.quote: On 9 July 1964, article 133 crashed while landing

incidents.summary: A-12 article 126 crash after takeoff due to wiring error.
incidents.quote: on 28 December 1965, article 126 crashed immediately after takeoff

incidents.summary: A-12 crash due to fuel gauge malfunction.
incidents.explanation: Fuel gauge malfunctioned and the aircraft ran out of fuel.
incidents.quote: on 5 January 1967, an A-12 crashed after a fuel gauge malfunctioned

incidents.summary: A-12 disappearance during test flight.
incidents.quote: On 4 June 1968 during a test flight from Kadena to check out a new engine, an A-12 disappeared
